title: Proofread every line students meet
statement: Proofread every line a student reads or hears, model answers first, since validators miss grammar slips and the repeated stock openers of machine writing.
example: One course repeated two stock openers across 11 think-alouds, and no validator caught it.
detail: Two proofreading sweeps on 2026-08-31 read only the surface prose of every string a child sees or hears, leaving out whatever a validator already owns (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0233-aug31-sweeps-prose-and-slotmap.qmd`). In one course the worst finding was in a spoken model answer, the kind a child imitates: a subject-verb error repeated at 5 paths; in the other, every think-aloud in one unit opened with the same clause and every one in a second unit with another, 11 verbatim repetitions in all, and none of the findings is caught by any current validator (the same file). A slip that recurred at one slot was recommended as one fix to its template, not four patches (the same file). An earlier course review found word-bank prompts that misuse vocabulary and read as unedited AI output (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0086-round2-feedback-brainlifts-2026-07-09.qmd`).

Small text defects matter when the course itself models quotation and evidence conventions.

the codebase's validators (`validate-contracts.mjs`, `validate-feedback.mjs`, `validate-component-text.mjs`) enforce em-dash/semicolon/ALL-CAPS/parens/slash-compound bans, field-shape, and pre-read rules, none of which cover subject-verb agreement, run-on sentences after quotes, filler-word punctuation consistency, or repeated sentences
